kindInfo.nfd: Names stored the macOS way (decomposed, NFD) are converted to the composed form (NFC) Windows expects, so accented and Japanese names look the same on both.
kindInfo.invalidChar: Characters Windows forbids in names (< > : " | ? * \) are replaced with an underscore.
kindInfo.trailingDotSpace: Dots and spaces at the end of a name are removed, since Windows drops them.
kindInfo.reserved: Names Windows reserves for devices, such as CON, NUL, COM1 or LPT1, with or without an extension, get an underscore added.
kindInfo.suspicious: Zero-width and text-direction characters are kept but reported, since they can disguise a name.
kindInfo.collision: Two names that differ only in upper and lower case, or that become the same once fixed, block the archive: Windows cannot keep both.
kindInfo.paths: Paths are made relative to the archive, and any path that would point outside it is left out.
kindInfo.pathTooLong: A path longer than Windows allows (a name over 255 characters, or a whole path over 260) is reported. The count covers only the path inside the archive; the folder the recipient extracts into makes it longer.
kindInfo.exclusions: What the exclusion patterns match is left out while “Leave out what the exclusion patterns match” is on. The list starts with system clutter from macOS, Windows and Linux, such as .DS_Store, ._ files, Thumbs.db and desktop.ini, and is edited in Settings.
kindInfo.duplicate: A file reached through more than one input is archived once.
kindInfo.emptyDirs: Empty folders are kept, or left out when you choose to prune them.
kindInfo.symlink: Symbolic links are ignored by default. They can be kept as Unix links, which Windows extracts as small text files, or followed so their targets are archived.
kindInfo.special: Sockets, pipes, devices and links that cannot be followed are left out and listed in the report. A folder that cannot be read is reported, and its originals are never moved to Trash or deleted.
kindInfo.dates: Modification times before 1980 or after 2107, which ZIP cannot store, are moved to the nearest date it can.
kindInfo.outputExists: The archive never includes itself, and an existing file is never replaced unless you allow it.

exclusions.hint: New jobs leave out what these patterns match, checked from the top. A glob without a slash matches a name in any folder; one with a slash is matched from the archive’s top level. A regular expression is matched against the whole path.
exclusions.empty: No patterns: new jobs leave nothing out.
exclusions.issueTarget: A glob ending in / matches folders. Choose Folders or Files and folders.
exclusionNote.dsStore: Finder’s view settings for a folder. Finder creates it again.
exclusionNote.macosx: Mac-only data left over from unzipping a ZIP made on a Mac. Not part of the files themselves.
exclusionNote.appleDoubleFiles: Mac-only data saved beside a file on a drive that isn’t Mac-formatted. ZipKit doesn’t keep such data.
exclusionNote.appleDoubleFolder: Mac-only data kept by a file server or a drive that isn’t Mac-formatted. ZipKit doesn’t keep such data.
exclusionNote.folderIcon: A folder’s custom icon in Finder. A ZIP can’t hold its image.
exclusionNote.spotlight: A drive’s Spotlight search index. macOS rebuilds it.
exclusionNote.revisions: Older versions of documents macOS saved on a drive. Only macOS can read them.
exclusionNote.temporaryItems: Temporary files macOS keeps on a drive.
exclusionNote.trashMac: A drive’s Trash (macOS). Holds what was deleted from that drive.
exclusionNote.fseventsd: macOS’s record of changes on a drive. Rebuilt as needed.
exclusionNote.apdisk: Settings an AirPort base station saved on a shared drive.
exclusionNote.timeMachine: Marks a drive as a Time Machine backup disk. Not a file of yours.
exclusionNote.volumeIcon: A drive’s custom icon in Finder. It belongs to the drive, not the files.
exclusionNote.localized: Tells Finder to show the folder’s name translated. Without it, the folder shows its own name.
exclusionNote.appleServer: An old Apple file server’s own records. Not files of yours.
exclusionNote.thumbs: Windows’ thumbnail cache for a folder. Windows creates it again.
exclusionNote.mediaCenterThumbs: Windows Media Center’s thumbnail cache. Rebuilt when needed.
exclusionNote.desktopIni: A folder’s icon and display name, set by Windows or a sync app. The files don’t need it.
exclusionNote.recycleBin: A drive’s Recycle Bin. Holds what was deleted from that drive.
exclusionNote.systemVolume: Windows’ restore points and search index for a drive. Only Windows can use them.
exclusionNote.trashLinux: A drive’s Trash (Linux). Holds what was deleted from that drive.
exclusionNote.kdeDirectory: A folder’s icon and view settings in KDE. The files don’t need it.
exclusionNote.nfs: A file deleted on a network share while still open. It disappears once closed.
exclusionNote.fuseHidden: A file deleted while still open (Linux). It disappears once closed.
exclusionNote.windowsMemory: Windows’ memory or hibernation file, often several gigabytes. Windows creates it again at startup.
exclusionNote.oldRecycleBin: A drive’s Recycle Bin from older Windows. Holds what was deleted from that drive.
exclusionNote.classicDesktop: Classic Mac OS’s record of a drive’s files and icons. The system rebuilds it.
exclusionNote.mobileBackups: Time Machine snapshots kept on the Mac itself (older macOS). Only Time Machine can use them.
